title: Ned Is Unsure
checkpoint: Phase 6 (School readiness) — the prefixes 'un-' and 'dis-' (sure → unsure, appear → disappear)
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 6 book for the beginnings 'un-' and 'dis-'. Cover the beginning with your finger and read the root word first, then uncover it — 'sure … unsure'. Talk about how that little beginning flips the meaning right round.

pages.text: Ned was unsure. His best stone had gone, and he did not see how.
pages.illustration: Ned the gold duckling at the pond edge staring at a small empty dip in the mud where a stone clearly used to sit. Shoulders down, beak down. Overcast grey-green — the flattest page in the book.

pages.text: It did not just go. It did disappear.
pages.illustration: The same empty dip in the mud, drawn closer and larger, with a faint dotted outline where the stone was. Ned's shadow falls across it. Quiet and a bit eerie.

pages.text: Olive said the pond was unsafe. Ned went in, and Ned got wet.
pages.illustration: Olive the plum owl on a branch with one wing up in warning; below her Ned already chest-deep in the pond, rings spreading out. Split the page between her calm and his splashing.

pages.text: He was undone. His best fluff was all stuck down flat.
pages.illustration: Ned standing on the bank dripping, down plastered flat so he looks half his normal size, water running off his tail. Nell the bee hovering nearby, trying hard not to laugh.

pages.text: “I disagree,” said Nell. “I do not think it went. I think it is under a reed.”
pages.illustration: Nell the sunflower-yellow bee hovering with one leg pointing firmly down, absolutely certain. Ned looking up at her with dawning hope. Colour floods back into the page here.

pages.text: So they went to unpack the reeds. Olive did dislike the mud, but she went in too.
pages.illustration: Nell pulling reed stems apart like curtains; Olive stepping into the shallows with an expression of deep distaste, one foot lifted high. Detailed reeds, brown water, comic dignity.

pages.text: There it was in the mud, half unseen. Ned was not unsure at all now.
pages.illustration: The stone half buried in dark mud, one polished grey curve catching the light. Ned's face right up close to it, eyes enormous. Warm light breaking through the reeds.

pages.text: He put it back. Then he sat on it, so it could not disappear on him.
pages.illustration: Ned sitting squarely and smugly on top of the stone at the water's edge, wings folded, immovable. Late gold light on the pond. Nell and Olive behind him, amused.
